version.changelog:

- Functionality and documentation remain unchanged.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its marketing purpose (Douyin/TikHub + DeepSeek analysis) but has packaging and permission inconsistencies and uses shell/child-process execution patterns that warrant caution before installing or running with real credentials.

dimensions.detail: The skill's described purpose (抖音/多平台爆款分析、AI 标题/脚本、商品/竞品分析) aligns with the code and declared network hosts (api.tikhub.io, api.deepseek.com, douyin.com). However there are metadata inconsistencies: top-level summary in the evaluation says "Required env vars: none" while manifest.yaml and SKILL.md require TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY. The bundle is not truly instruction-only (there is a ~49KB scripts/marketing_hub.js), despite the earlier "No install spec — this is an instruction-only skill" statement. These mismatches reduce confidence in the packaging quality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md/README instruct cloning the repo and setting two API keys (TikHub, DeepSeek), and files are persisted under scripts/memory/*.json. The runtime instructions and code access only the declared services and write to the skill workspace. They do not, in the visible files, request unrelated credentials or system files. That said, SKILL.md and the code allow running a real browser, downloading/processing videos, and storing scraped data locally — behavior consistent with the stated purpose but worth noting for privacy of scraped content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external download/install URL and no package manager install step; the skill is distributed as repo code you run with Node.js. This is lower risk than arbitrary remote installers. However the manifest and README claim no extra dependencies while the code expects system binaries (chrome, ffmpeg, whisper) to be present — so the runtime environment must provide these binaries.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The functionality reasonably requires two API keys (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY) which appear in manifest and SKILL.md and are used by the code. But the top-level metadata reported 'Required env vars: none' (incoherent). No other unrelated credentials are requested. Still, the code will read environment variables and may fallback to a local config.js file; ensure you do not place unrelated secrets in that file or the skill workspace (scripts/config.js or scripts/.env).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and the skill does not claim to modify other skills or global agent settings. It writes to its own scripts/memory/ directory (declared in manifest) which is coherent with its memory feature. The manifest allows running subprocesses (node, curl, ffmpeg, whisper, chrome, pkill) — which is functionally justified for scraping, video/audio processing and cleaning up browser processes, but subprocess execution increases attack surface (see guidance).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the advertised marketing/analysis features, but there are packaging inconsistencies and it executes system commands which increases risk. Before installing or running it:
- Prefer running it in an isolated environment (container or VM) to contain potential misuse of subprocesses (chrome/ffmpeg/pkill).
- Only supply TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY that are scoped/minimal; avoid reusing high-privilege or long-lived secrets.
- Inspect the full scripts/marketing_hub.js for any command invocations that include user-supplied input (possible shell injection points) — if you cannot audit it, avoid running with real credentials.
- Keep the skill workspace (scripts/) separate from any sensitive files; do not store other secrets in scripts/config.js or scripts/.env.
- If you need higher assurance, request the repository/source checksum or run the code in a disposable environment and observe network traffic to confirm only the declared hosts are contacted.
